winner.title: Mtuzi Wa Samaki

evidence.authenticity: Intro explains Zanzibar origin, spice-trade roots and clove production; coconut-tomato-tamarind base is traditional. Bell peppers and optional garam masala/curry powder are a looser, generic take.
evidence.precision: 1 of 10 ingredients has a weight (fish 2-2.5 lb); onion, peppers and tomatoes are unsized; no pan size or temperatures. Doneness cues on 3 of 9 steps (onion translucent, fish cooked through, simmer 6-8 min).
evidence.testing: No test-kitchen process and little reasoning beyond a note that firm fish holds up; searing then removing the fish is not explained.
evidence.photos: imagesOnPage 45 but stepImagesInSchema 0; not confirmed as process photos, so scored as hero shots only.
evidence.efficiency: About 35 minutes total, sensible sequence: sear fish, build sauce, return fish.
evidence.access: Tamarind paste is listed with a lemon juice alternative; garam masala or curry powder is easy to find. All else is at a US grocery.

winner.why: Best roots and context, with a more complete method than Great British Chefs, but still short on precision and photos, so below 60.

runnerUp.title: Mchuzi wa samaki (Tanzanian coconut fish curry)

evidence.authenticity: Named as the local dish with a tomato, coconut and tamarind base; but salmon plus hake and generic curry powder are Westernized choices, and little regional context.
evidence.precision: Metric weights for fish and coconut milk (3 of 13 ingredients with weights); 'handful' of coriander; no pan size; 1 sensory cue; mostly minutes only.
evidence.testing: Professional recipe site editorial kitchen, but only 2 ratings and no explanation of reasoning.
evidence.photos: No step images in schema; imagesOnPage 14 with no confirmed process shots.
evidence.efficiency: 50 minutes; a 30-minute coconut simmer before the fish is longer than needed.
evidence.access: Everything is available in a US grocery.

runnerUp.why: Metric weights and a cleaner structure, but a Westernized fish choice and no doneness cues.

candidates.disqualified: Near word-for-word copy of the Whats4Eats and AFN recipe; user submission with 1 rating.
